subQuestions.questionText:
The MAIN reason for the development of informal settlements in South African cities is …

A urban-rural migration.
B poor town planning.
C rapid rural-urban migration.
D high crime rates.

In the concentric zone model, the zone located DIRECTLY next to the CBD is called the …

A rural-urban fringe.
B zone of transition.
C residential zone.
D industrial zone.

When two or more cities expand and merge together to form one continuous urban area, the result is called a …

A metropolis.
B megalopolis.
C conurbation.
D suburb.

An example of a social push factor that causes rural-urban migration is …

A employment opportunities in cities.
B better education in urban areas.
C improved health care in cities.
D farm attacks and killings in rural areas.

options.D: farm attacks and killings in rural areas.

subQuestions.questionText:
Access to better health care and education in urban areas is an example of a/an …

A urban pull factor.
B rural push factor.
C natural factor.
D economic push factor.

The area from which a settlement draws its customers and users is known as its …

A sphere of influence.
B threshold population.
C settlement function.
D land-use zone.

The land-use zone at the edge of a city, where farming and industrial activities exist side by side, is known as the …

A CBD.
B zone of transition.
C rural-urban fringe.
D suburb.

Which ONE of the following is a characteristic of INFORMAL settlements?

A Limited access to basic services such as electricity and clean water
B Formal housing with registered title deeds
C Planned street layouts with kerbs and pavements
D High land values and large stand sizes

options.A: Limited access to basic services such as electricity and clean water
options.B: Formal housing with registered title deeds
options.C: Planned street layouts with kerbs and pavements
options.D: High land values and large stand sizes

subQuestions.questionText:

As the order of a central place increases, the number of settlements of that order ___________.

Refer to the extract about rural-urban migration in the question paper.

Define the concept rural-urban migration.
subQuestions.memoText:
Rural-urban migration is the movement of people (1 mark) from rural areas to urban areas. (1 mark)
[Full definition = 2 marks; part mark: 'movement of people' without specifying direction = 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the extract about rural-urban migration in the question paper.

State ONE social push factor in a rural area that causes people to migrate to urban areas.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE of: Farm killings/attacks; Poverty; Lack of job opportunities. (1 mark each)

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the extract about rural-urban migration in the question paper.

State TWO basic services that are more accessible in urban areas.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO of (1 mark each): Piped/potable water; Electricity; Sanitation; Refuse and waste removal; Health care (accept examples); Social welfare; Housing; Education; Safety and security.

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the extract about rural-urban migration and the photograph of the urban area in the question paper.

Explain how rural-urban migration can create challenges regarding housing in urban areas. Give TWO challenges.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fully explained challenge. Any TWO of:
• The demand for housing cannot be met [because too many people arrive at once]. (2)
• There is a shortage of suitable land [for new housing development]. (2)
• Limited municipal budgets [means fewer houses can be built to accommodate migrants]. (2)

Part marking: 1 mark for stating the challenge without explaining the cause.

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the extract about rural-urban migration in the question paper.

Suggest THREE intervention strategies that the government can use to decrease rural-urban migration.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per strategy (strategy + explanation). Any THREE of:
• Create more/better employment opportunities (accept examples). (2)
• Promote commercial farming. (2)
• Develop/upskill workers (accept examples). (2)
• Provide credit facilities/loans/subsidies to farmers. (2)
• Effective land reform programmes (accept examples). (2)
• Decentralise industries/businesses. (2)
• Develop ecotourism (accept examples). (2)
• Organise festivals/recreational activities (accept examples). (2)
• Advertising/marketing of the area. (2)
• Providing basic services (accept examples). (2)
• Improvement of infrastructure (accept examples). (2)
• Create incentives to encourage people to limit rural-urban migration. (2)
• Resettlement of people in agriculturally suitable areas. (2)

subQuestions.questionText:
Study the photograph of a land-use area in the question paper.

Identify the location of Area B in relation to the urban area.
subQuestions.memoText: Outskirts/Periphery of the urban area. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Study the photograph of a land-use area in the question paper.

State TWO economic activities visible in the photograph.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO of (1 mark each): Agriculture/Farming; Industries/Manufacturing.

subQuestions.questionText:
Study the photograph of a land-use area in the question paper.

How does the economic activity at Area B benefit from its location in the rural-urban fringe? Explain TWO ways.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per benefit. Any TWO of:
• Cheaper land values [so the business saves on overheads]. (2)
• Enough vacant land for expansion [room to grow without relocating]. (2)
• Access to infrastructure (accept examples). (2)
• Raw materials from nearby farms [reducing transport costs]. (2)
• Close to labour force [workers from surrounding residential areas]. (2)
• Access to flat land [easier and cheaper to construct]. (2)
• Access to water [for industrial processes]. (2)
• Access to nearby markets [reducing delivery distances]. (2)
• Less traffic congestion [compared to the CBD]. (2)

subQuestions.questionText:
Study the photograph of a land-use area in the question paper.

What positive impact does the economic activity at Area B have on the local community? Explain TWO impacts.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per impact. Any TWO of:
• Provides employment opportunities [reducing local unemployment]. (2)
• Upskilling of local labour force (accept examples). (2)
• Social upliftment programmes [e.g. bursaries, sport facilities]. (2)
• Infrastructural improvements (accept examples). (2)
• Improved services (accept examples). (2)
• Prevents people moving out of the area [retaining population]. (2)
• Increases standard of living [higher incomes]. (2)
• Closer to work [reduces commuting time and cost]. (2)
• Availability of finished goods [locally produced products accessible]. (2)
• Improves buying power [wages circulate in local economy]. (2)
• Multiplier effect (accept examples). (2)
• Lowers prices of goods (accept examples). (2)

subQuestions.questionText:
Study the photograph of a land-use area in the question paper.

How has the recent expansion of large cities changed the rural-urban fringe? Explain TWO ways.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per way. Any TWO of:
• Decreases land used for farming (accept examples). (2)
• Urban functions now dominate [residential and commercial replace agricultural land]. (2)
• Change in variety/type of urban functions. (2)
• Increases the value of land. (2)
• Increase in the number of people. (2)
• Increase in crime. (2)
• Services are under pressure. (2)
• More buildings (accept examples). (2)
• Urban sprawl [uncontrolled outward growth]. (2)
• Increased traffic [congestion on roads]. (2)
• Increased levels of pollution (accept examples). (2)
• Aesthetic beauty of the land-use zone is diminished. (2)
• Destruction of biodiversity/ecosystems. (2)
• Increased soil erosion. (2)
• Less fertile soil. (2)
• Increased run-off. (2)
• Water table lowered. (2)

subQuestions.questionText:
Study the photograph of a settlement in the question paper.

Identify ONE characteristic of the settlement that is visible in the photograph.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE of: Limited infrastructure (accept examples); Prefabricated/makeshift materials (accept examples); High building density; Limited space; Small houses; Lack of planning; Lack of basic services (accept examples). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Study the extract about informal settlements in the question paper.

State TWO negative social impacts mentioned in the extract.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO of (1 mark each): Tiny spaces (lack of privacy); Overcrowding; Overlapping structures (fire hazard); Diseases.

subQuestions.questionText:
Study the photograph and extract about informal settlements in the question paper.

Give TWO economic reasons for the rapid growth of informal settlements.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per reason. Any TWO of:
• Increased unemployment [people cannot afford formal housing]. (2)
• Increased poverty [insufficient income to pay rent or a bond]. (2)
• High inflation rate [rising cost of living]. (2)
• High price/rent of formal houses [beyond reach of low-income earners]. (2)
• People cannot afford formal housing. (2)
• Salary cuts [reduced income forces people into cheaper alternatives]. (2)
• Budget constraints [government cannot build enough RDP houses]. (2)

subQuestions.questionText:
Study the photograph and extract about informal settlements in the question paper.

Write a paragraph explaining why the government has failed to assist communities living in informal settlements.
subQuestions.memoText:
Write a paragraph. Award 2 marks per point (problem stated + reason/explanation). Maximum 8 marks (any 4 points).

Acceptable points:
• Government did not provide low-cost housing because of a shortage of available land or budget constraints. (2)
• No basic services/amenities were supplied due to budget shortfalls. (2)
• No basic infrastructure was built due to a lack of skilled personnel. (2)
• Government did not create enough job opportunities because of a lack of investment. (2)
• Inadequate policing to combat crime due to poor planning. (2)
• Government did not allocate sufficient finance for improving conditions due to budget constraints. (2)
• Corruption which led to misappropriation of finances/budget shortfalls. (2)
• Unqualified people managed projects (resulting in delays) due to nepotism/cronyism. (2)
• Limited programmes for upskilling/training of communities due to budget constraints. (2)
• Land tenure issues forced people to remain in informal settlements. (2)

Part marking (max 4 marks if no reasons given): 1 mark for each problem stated without explanation.

subQuestions.questionText:
Agriculture, fishing and forestry are examples of … economic activities.

A tertiary
B primary
C secondary
D quaternary

Which ONE of the following is an example of a SECONDARY economic activity?

A Manufacturing
B Fishing
C Teaching
D Nursing

A business that operates without being registered and does not pay taxes to SARS is part of the …

A formal sector.
B public sector.
C informal sector.
D corporate sector.

The Maputo Corridor Spatial Development Initiative (MCSPI) is MAINLY designed to …

A reduce population growth along the corridor.
B stimulate economic development along a transport corridor.
C decrease urbanisation in Gauteng.
D improve the environment along the corridor.

options.A: reduce population growth along the corridor.
options.B: stimulate economic development along a transport corridor.
options.D: improve the environment along the corridor.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following is a PHYSICAL factor that promotes commercial farming?

A Proximity to markets
B Availability of capital
C Fertile soil
D Skilled labour force

The disadvantage of subsistence farming compared to commercial farming is that it …

A uses modern technology.
B produces surpluses for export.
C employs many farm workers.
D produces only enough food for the farmer's household.

options.D: produces only enough food for the farmer's household.

subQuestions.questionText:
A Spatial Development Initiative (SDI) aims to …

A reduce migration into cities.
B develop economic activity along a transport corridor.
C create conservation areas.
D limit foreign investment.

options.B: develop economic activity along a transport corridor.

subQuestions.questionText:
The Maputo Corridor connects South Africa's Gauteng region to the port city of …

A Durban.
B Cape Town.
C Beira.
D Maputo.

Classify the following statements as relating to EITHER:
Y = Commercial farming
Z = Subsistence farming

Write only Y or Z next to the question number.

'Uses modern machinery and large-scale irrigation systems.'

Classify the following statements as relating to EITHER:
Y = Commercial farming
Z = Subsistence farming

Write only Y or Z next to the question number.

'Produces crops mainly for the family's own consumption.'

Classify the following statements as relating to EITHER:
Y = Commercial farming
Z = Subsistence farming

Write only Y or Z next to the question number.

'Uses traditional farming methods on small plots of land.'

Classify the following statements as relating to EITHER:
Y = Commercial farming
Z = Subsistence farming

Write only Y or Z next to the question number.

'Produces a surplus of crops that is sold to make a profit.'

Classify the following statements as relating to EITHER:
Y = Commercial farming
Z = Subsistence farming

Write only Y or Z next to the question number.

'Exports produce to foreign markets.'

Classify the following statements as relating to EITHER:
Y = Commercial farming
Z = Subsistence farming

Write only Y or Z next to the question number.

'Located mainly in former homeland areas and relies on seasonal rainfall.'

Classify the following statements as relating to EITHER:
Y = Commercial farming

Write only Y or Z next to the question number.

Study the graph showing sugar cane production in South Africa in the question paper.

Read off the percentage of sugar cane that is processed into sugar.

Study the map/graph showing sugar cane production in South Africa in the question paper.

Name TWO South African provinces where sugar cane is mainly produced.
subQuestions.memoText: KwaZulu-Natal (1 mark); Mpumalanga (1 mark). (Both required for 2 marks.)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO physical factors that promote the growing of sugar cane.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO of (1 mark each): Subtropical climate conditions; High temperatures; High rainfall; Frost-free area; Well-drained/fertile soils.

subQuestions.questionText:
Study the extract about sugar cane farming in the question paper.

Explain why sugar cane farming is important to small towns and rural villages. Give TWO reasons.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per reason. Any TWO of:
• Provides employment on farms and in sugar mills [reducing local unemployment]. (2)
• Multiplier effect/stimulates the economy (accept examples). (2)
• Provides income for small-scale farmers [improving livelihoods]. (2)
• Raw materials for secondary activities (accept examples). (2)
• Improves infrastructure (accept examples). (2)
• Small towns/rural villages are partly or entirely dependent on sugar cane farming. (2)
• Improved standard of living/quality of life (accept examples). (2)
• Creates access to markets for rural communities. (2)

subQuestions.questionText:
Study the extract about sugar cane farming in the question paper.

Explain THREE economic factors that have a negative impact on sugar production in South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per factor. Any THREE of:
• The sugar tax has decreased demand for sugar [consumers buy less sugar]. (2)
• Fluctuating sugar prices limit investment [uncertainty discourages farmers from expanding]. (2)
• Increase in cost of exports [making South African sugar less competitive]. (2)
• Demand for sugar cane in Southern Africa has decreased (accept examples). (2)
• Higher production costs (accept examples such as fuel, fertiliser, labour). (2)
• Load shedding decreases production [machinery cannot operate during power cuts]. (2)
• Lack of subsidies in South Africa [unlike competing countries that receive government support]. (2)
• Labour strikes decrease production [work stoppages result in crop losses]. (2)

subQuestions.questionText:
Study the extract about the Maputo Corridor Spatial Development Initiative (MCSPI) in the question paper.

Name ONE foreign country that forms part of the MCSPI.

Study the extract about the Maputo Corridor Spatial Development Initiative (MCSPI) in the question paper.

From the extract, state the purpose of the MCSPI.
subQuestions.memoText: To rebuild their economies and restore trade and investment ties. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Study the extract about the Maputo Corridor Spatial Development Initiative (MCSPI) in the question paper.

Identify the core industrial region that is linked to the MCSPI.

Study the extract about the Maputo Corridor Spatial Development Initiative (MCSPI) in the question paper.

Explain how the MCSPI will create business opportunities for underdeveloped communities. Give TWO ways.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per way. Any TWO of:
• Improved infrastructural development [roads/rails make business logistics easier] (accept examples). (2)
• Increased volumes of traffic [more customers and trade opportunities for local businesses]. (2)
• The route becomes safer [encouraging more investment and travel]. (2)
• Promotes entrepreneurial opportunities (accept examples). (2)
• Increased skills of local people [through employment and training]. (2)
• Multiplier effect (increased buying power) [more jobs lead to more spending in local economy] (accept examples). (2)
• Job creation [providing income to previously unemployed communities]. (2)
• Promotes trade (accept examples). (2)

subQuestions.questionText:
Study the extract about the Maputo Corridor Spatial Development Initiative (MCSPI) in the question paper.

Write a paragraph explaining how the upgrading of different types of infrastructure positively impacts on trade.
subQuestions.memoText:
Write a paragraph. Award 2 marks per point (type of infrastructure + how it impacts trade). Maximum 8 marks (any 4 points).

Acceptable points:
• Improved railways result in cheaper transport of goods [lower logistics costs]. (2)
• Improved roads will facilitate rapid transport of goods [faster deliveries]. (2)
• Expanding the port encourages export/import of bulky goods [more cargo capacity]. (2)
• Improving port facilities will increase the volume/efficiency of export of goods. (2)
• More accessibility by ports/roads/rail improves trade (accept examples). (2)
• Improved power supply will improve production [fewer interruptions to manufacturing]. (2)
• Improved communication networks improve trade relations [easier to coordinate supply chains]. (2)

Part marking (max 4 marks if no impact explained): 1 mark for naming the type of infrastructure without explaining its impact on trade.

subQuestions.questionText:
Study the extract about a street vendor in the question paper.

Name the economic sector to which this vendor belongs, as referred to in the extract.

Study the extract about a street vendor in the question paper.

From the extract, state ONE reason why the vendor does not operate from a formal business.

Study the extract about a street vendor in the question paper.

Quote ONE example from the extract that shows how the government challenges informal traders.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE of (must be a direct quote from the extract): 'regular raids'; 'goods are seized'; 'fines are issued'. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Study the extract about a street vendor in the question paper.

Give ONE reason why informal businesses are regarded as part of the shadow economy.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE of (2 marks each): They do not pay taxes to SARS. (2); Unregistered businesses [operate outside the formal legal framework]. (2)

subQuestions.questionText:
Study the extract about a street vendor in the question paper.

Explain how the economy benefits from the informal sector. Give TWO ways.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per way. Any TWO of:
• Creates jobs [reducing unemployment without government expenditure]. (2)
• Reduces dependence on the state (accept examples). (2)
• Goods are cheaper [informal traders have lower overheads]. (2)
• Services are affordable (accept examples). (2)
• They buy goods/merchandise from formal businesses [supporting formal sector revenue]. (2)
• Creation of new skills (accept examples). (2)
• They pay VAT [contributing to government revenue]. (2)
• Reduces crime [by providing livelihoods for unemployed people]. (2)

subQuestions.questionText:
Study the extract about a street vendor in the question paper.

Suggest THREE incentives that the government can provide to regulate the informal sector.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per incentive. Any THREE of:
• Reduce taxes [for newly registered informal businesses]. (2)
• Affordable/free registration fees [to make formalisation accessible]. (2)
• Provide access to capital/loans [to help businesses grow]. (2)
• Skills training (accept examples). (2)
• Allow informal businesses to operate from home [reducing overhead costs]. (2)
• Effective policing/no harassment [creating a fair and safe trading environment]. (2)
• Offer affordable rentals on premises [in designated trading areas]. (2)
• Employment benefits to workers in the informal sector. (2)
• Partnerships between formal and informal sectors. (2)
• Provision of facilities (accept examples such as market stalls, ablution blocks). (2)
• Provide services (accept examples). (2)
